QuestionStmt.S: If the shortest distance between the lines $$\frac{x-k}{2} = \frac{y-4}{3} = \frac{z-3}{4}$$ and $$\frac{x-2}{4} = \frac{y-4}{6} = \frac{z-7}{8}$$ is $$\frac{13}{\sqrt{29}},$$ then $k =$

Solution.S:
The lines are parallel as direction vectors are $\vec{b} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$ and $4\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} + 8\hat{k} = 2\vec{b}$.

Points: $\vec{a_1} = k\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$, $\vec{a_2} = 2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}$.

Shortest distance between parallel lines:

$$d = \frac{|\vec{b} \times (\vec{a_2} - \vec{a_1})|}{|\vec{b}|}$$

Here $\vec{a_2} - \vec{a_1} = (2 - k)\hat{i} + 0\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$.

Compute cross product:

$$\vec{b} \times (\vec{a_2} - \vec{a_1}) = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 2-k & 0 & 4 \end{vmatrix}$$

$$= \hat{i}(3 \cdot 4 - 4 \cdot 0) - \hat{j}(2 \cdot 4 - 4(2-k)) + \hat{k}(2 \cdot 0 - 3(2-k))$$

$$= \hat{i}(12) - \hat{j}(8 - 8 + 4k) + \hat{k}(-6 + 3k)$$

$$= 12\hat{i} - 4k\hat{j} + (3k - 6)\hat{k}$$

Magnitude:

$$|\vec{b} \times (\vec{a_2} - \vec{a_1})| = \sqrt{144 + 16k^2 + (3k - 6)^2}$$

Given $d = \frac{13}{\sqrt{29}}$, $|\vec{b}| = \sqrt{4 + 9 + 16} = \sqrt{29}$.

Thus:

$$\frac{\sqrt{144 + 16k^2 + (3k - 6)^2}}{\sqrt{29}} = \frac{13}{\sqrt{29}}$$

$$\Rightarrow \sqrt{144 + 16k^2 + 9k^2 - 36k + 36} = 13$$

$$\sqrt{25k^2 - 36k + 180} = 13$$

Squaring: $25k^2 - 36k + 180 = 169$

$25k^2 - 36k + 11 = 0$

Solving: $k = 1$ or $k = 11/25$.

From options, $k = 1$.

Thus the correct option is A: 1.
